label: Small Biotech IND — Clinical Overview (2.5)
description: Module 2.5 Clinical Overview with benefit-risk for NovaTide-1 Phase 1 (DLBCL).

inputs.mechanism_of_action: Simultaneously binds CD3 on T cells and CD20 on malignant B cells, redirecting cytotoxic T cells to kill tumor cells via perforin/granzyme pathway
inputs.proposed_dosage: 3 mg/kg IV weekly × 8, then every 2 weeks (with step-up dosing in Cycle 1)
inputs.target_population: Adults (≥18 years) with R/R DLBCL after ≥2 prior lines of therapy
inputs.clinical_pharmacology_summary: NovaTide-1 exhibits linear pharmacokinetics in the 0.1–10 mg/kg range. Mean terminal half-life is 6.2 days. Steady-state achieved by Cycle 3. No clinically meaningful drug-drug interactions anticipated based on mechanism. Exposure-response modeling suggests the 3 mg/kg dose provides >90% CD20 receptor occupancy.
inputs.secondary_endpoints: Median duration of response not reached at 4.2 months median follow-up. PFS at 6 months: 61% (95% CI: 45–74%). MRD negativity observed in 4/6 CR patients.
inputs.patient_reported_outcomes: EORTC QLQ-C30 showed stable global health status through Cycle 4. Transient decrease in physical functioning during CRS episodes, recovering within 7 days.
inputs.serious_adverse_events: SAE rate: 22% (16/73). Most common: CRS (Grade 3, n=4), febrile neutropenia (n=3), tumor lysis syndrome (n=2). All SAEs resolved.
inputs.deaths_summary: No treatment-related deaths. Two deaths due to disease progression.
inputs.lab_findings: Transient lymphopenia (expected pharmacology). B-cell depletion confirmed in all patients. Transient elevations in IL-6, ferritin consistent with CRS. No hepatotoxicity signal.
inputs.severity_of_condition: R/R DLBCL is a life-threatening malignancy with median OS of 6 months after failure of ≥2 prior lines
inputs.unmet_medical_need: High — limited options after CAR-T failure or for CAR-T ineligible patients
inputs.efficacy_strength: Preliminary ORR of 52% with 14% CR rate in heavily pretreated population; consistent with bispecific antibody class
inputs.safety_profile: Manageable with step-up dosing and CRS mitigation protocols; no unexpected safety signals
inputs.risk_mitigation: Step-up dosing, mandatory hospitalization for first 2 doses, tocilizumab premedication protocol, REMS-like distribution
inputs.benefit_risk_conclusion: The preliminary benefit-risk profile of NovaTide-1 is favorable for continued development. The observed efficacy (52% ORR) in a population with limited options justifies the manageable safety risks, particularly with the step-up dosing mitigation strategy.
